messages.author: 94bbbe52a1a2ee84
messages.subject: MQM FDR for eQTL
parts:
Dear Karl, dear community,

I am using mqmscanall for an eQTL with 236 transcripts and want to estimate the false discovery rate of QTL peaks at certain LOD tresholds using the mqmscanfdr function. I run into three problems that might or might not be related:

1) a warning message that warns me about QTL at certain marker locations having negative log-likelihood

2) an error message: error in res[[y]][ , 3]: incorrect number of dimensions

3) another warning message, but this one is from a function in the snow package for multithreading and might be related to error (2): "scheduled core 1 encountered error in user code, all values of the job will be affected"

Here is the code:

males_jitter_expression_imp <- fill.geno(male_jitter_expression, method="imp")  # fill in missing genotype data in QTL object "male_jitter_expression" with 142 individuals and 236 phenotypes (only phenotypes are transcript counts)

males_autocofactors <- mqmautocofactors(males_jitter_expression_imp, 50) # automatic cofactor selection

library(snow) # for multithreading

males_mqmscan<-mqmscanall(males_jitter_expression_imp, cofactors=males_autocofactors, window.size=10, n.cluster=4) # this works fine

mqmplot.multitrait(males_mqmscan, type="image") # these plots both look fine
mqmplot.circle(males_jitter_expression_imp,males_mqmscan)

males_mqmscan_fdr<-mqmscanfdr(males_jitter_expression_imp, mqmscanall, cofactors=males_autocofactors, n.perm=1000, n.cluster=4)

warning and errors (there are actually many many more negative QTL likelihood warnings, I just show a few as an example):

WARNING: Negative QTLlikelihood=-180.261692 versus BASE MODEL: -3591.549562
This applies to the QTL at 137
WARNING: Negative QTLlikelihood=-187.546979 versus BASE MODEL: -3591.549562
This applies to the QTL at 140
WARNING: Negative QTLlikelihood=-61.708500 versus BASE MODEL: -3591.549562
This applies to the QTL at 140
WARNING: Negative QTLlikelihood=-40.685421 versus BASE MODEL: -3591.549562
This applies to the QTL at 140
WARNING: Negative QTLlikelihood=-32.820216 versus BASE MODEL: -3591.549562
This applies to the QTL at 140
Error in res[[y]][, 3] : incorrect number of dimensions
In addition: Warning message:
In mclapply(boots, snowCoreALL, all.data = all.data, scanfunction = scanfunction,  :
  scheduled core 1 encountered error in user code, all values of the job will be affected

Any help is highly appreciated, thank you in advance.

best,

Thomas

messages.author: 92292fc48bf46044
messages.subject: Re: MQM FDR for eQTL
parts:
Dear thomas,

This error is usually due to the genetic map having issues, which could be due to many markers (2000+) or due to many double recombinations between markers which are close to eachother.
Normally it helps to find a subset of markers which gives you a good genetic map, but which does not overload the algorithm.

I have never seen the warning message: "scheduled core 1 encountered error in user code" before.
To debug this bug, I would need your input dataset, and the code you are using to re-create the same error

To send your dataset and code, reach me on: Danny....@gmail.com

of course data and code will be handled confidential

Kind regards,
Danny Arends

messages.author: 94bbbe52a1a2ee84
messages.subject: Re: MQM FDR for eQTL
parts:
Update:

The third error actually only occured when the function crashed with an error or when you cancel it yourself during computation. Error 1 and 2 are related and were caused by two specific phenotypes (transcripts) that had negative LOD scores, which I removed and then it worked fine. I could not find map density to be a problem, but it might be for other people.

Also, at first, when the negative likelihood occured in the permutations. I changed the scanmqmfdr code a little (using tryCatch()) so that it keeps going but returns a message whenever the error happens. This helped resolving error and also allowed me to do some preliminary analysis before actually debugging. In my case, the error occured always because permutated LOD scores were very low and occasionally dipped below zero. I am not sure how strong the effect of skipping the error will be on the final outcome, but since these weren't going to be significant peaks in the permutation above a certain LOD treshold, I do not expect them to lower the number of permutated false positives and thus make the FDR cut-offs less conservative. However, you want to find out what traits in your observed data are causing this problem rather than ignore error messages.

best,

Thomas
